<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="68.174.1.21" /></noinclude><section begin="par52"/>the {{GHGterm|perfect}} of the active (''Piʿ̄l''). The {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} of the first syllable is, however, with one exception (see m), always attenuated to ''ĭ'' in the {{GHGterm|perfect}}. In the second syllable, ''ă'' has been retained in the majority of cases, so that the conjugation should more correctly be called ''Piʿal;'' but very frequently<ref>So in all verbs which end in ''Nûn'', and in almost all which end in ''Lamed'' (Olsh. p. 538). Barth is probably right in supposing ({{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} 1894, p. 1 ff.) that the vowels of the strengthened perfects have been influenced by the {{GHGterm|imperfect}}.</ref> this ''ă'' also is attenuated to ''ĭ'', which is then regularly lengthened to ''ē'', under the influence of the tone. Cf. in Aram. {{GHGheb|text=קַטֵּל}}; but in Biblical Aramaic almost always {{GHGheb|text=קַטִּל}}. On the three cases in which ''ă'' before a final {{GHGheb|text=ר}} or {{GHGheb|text=ס}} has passed into {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}, see below, l.—Hence, for the ''3rd sing. masc. perfect'', there arise forms like {{GHGheb|text=אִבַּד}}, {{GHGheb|text=לִמַּד}}, {{GHGheb|text=קִדַּשׁ}}; {{GHGheb|text=גִּדֵּף}}, {{GHGheb|text=כִּבֵּד}}, &c.—Before afformatives beginning with a consonant, however, ''ă'' is always retained, thus {{GHGheb|text=קִטַּ֫לְתָּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=קִטַּלְתֶּם}}, {{GHGheb|text=קִטַּ֫לְנוּ}}, &c. In the ''infinitives'' ({{GHGterm|absol.}} {{GHGheb|text=קַטֹּל}}, obscured from ''qaṭṭâl''; {{GHGterm|constr.}} {{GHGheb|text=קַטֵּל}}), {{GHGterm|imperfect}} ({{GHGheb|text=יְקַטֵּל}}), {{GHGterm|imperative}} ({{GHGheb|text=קַטֵּל}}), and {{GHGterm|participle}} ({{GHGheb|text=מְקַטֵּל}}) the original ''ă'' of the first syllable reappears throughout. The vocal {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} of the preformatives is weakened from a short vowel; cf. the Arabic imperfect ''yŭqăttĭl'', participle ''mŭqăttĭl''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|b}}
The {{GHGterm|passive}} ({{GHGterm|Puʿal}}) is distinguished by the obscure vowel ''ŭ'', or very rarely ''ŏ'', in the first syllable, and ''ŏ'' (in pause ''ā'') always in the second. In Arabic, also, the passives are formed throughout with ''ŭ'' in the first syllable. The inflexion of both these conjugations is analogous to that of {{GHGterm|Qal}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|c}}
Rem. 1. The preformative {{GHGheb|text=מְ‍}}, which in the remaining conjugations also is the prefix of the participle, is probably connected with the interrogative or indefinite (cf. § 37) pronoun {{GHGheb|text=מִי|translate=quis? quicunque}} (fem. i.e. neuter, {{GHGheb|text=מָה}}); cf. {{GHGpar|85|e}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|d}}
2. The Dageš ''forte'', which according to the above is characteristic of the whole of {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} and {{GHGterm|Puʿal}}, is often omitted (independently of verbs ''middle guttural'', {{GHGpar|64|d}}) when the middle radical has {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} under it (cf. {{GHGpar|20|m}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שִׁלְחָה}} for {{GHGheb|text=שִׁלְּחָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=17|verse=17}}; {{GHGheb|text=בִּקְשֻׁ֫הוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=15|verse=15}} (but in the {{GHGterm|imperative}} always {{GHGheb|text=בַּקְּשׁוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=28|verse=7}}, &c.), and so always in {{GHGheb|text=הַלְלוּ|translate=praise}}. The vocal character of the {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} under the ''litera dagessanda'' is sometimes in such cases (according to {{GHGpar|10|h}}) expressly emphasized by its taking the form of a {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph}}, as in {{GHGheb|text=לֻֽקֳחָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=23}}, with {{GHGheb|text=־ֳ}} owing to the influence of the preceding ''u'', cf. {{GHGheb|text=פָּֽעֳלוֹ}} for {{GHGheb|text=פָּעְלוֹ}}, &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=16}}. In the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} and {{GHGterm|participle}} the {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} under the preformatives ({{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-Pathaḥ}} under {{GHGheb|text=א}} in the ''1st sing. imperfect'') serves at the same time as a characteristic of both conjugations ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=26|verse=14}} f.).

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|e}}
3. According to the convincing suggestion of Böttcher<ref>As Mayer Lambert observes, the same view was already expressed by Ibn Ǵanâḥ (see above, {{GHGpar|3|d}}) in the ''Kitāb el-lumaʿ'', p. 161. Cf. especially Barth, ‘Das passive Qal und seine Participien,’ in the {{GHGcite|title=Festschrift zum Jubiläum Hildesheimer}} (Berlin, 1890), p. 145 ff.</ref> ({{GHGcite|title=Ausführliches Lehrbuch}}, {{GHGpar|904|ff}}. and § 1022), many supposed perfects of {{GHGterm|Puʿal}} are in reality<section end="par52"/><noinclude>
